data.title: Long Table
data.statNote: More than dinner, it's a long evening.
data.description: Where ten strangers, one cook, and a long evening meet under low light. Twice a month, by application.
data.bigMeta: Twice a month, ten strangers, one cook, one long table. By application.

data.title:
A note
before
we sit.
paragraphs: We started Long Table in a borrowed kitchen, with six chairs we'd carried up the stairs, and the conviction that an evening is more than the food on the plates.
Three years on we've seated almost two thousand strangers across nine cities, and we've learned that the chairs are sometimes the most important part.
This deck is the small handbook we send our hosts before each edition. It is also, quietly, an invitation.
data.source: founders · written from a kitchen in Lisbon, November 2025

cards.title:
A Plate
of Quiet
cards.text: Eight courses cooked entirely on a single induction ring. The room agreed not to use phones for the entire evening, and almost kept the agreement.

cards.title:
A Soup
of Letters
cards.text: A reading evening, with a single course served slowly. Four guest writers, one bowl per person, and the longest pause we have ever held between courses.

cards.title:
December
Edition
cards.text: A long winter dinner. Twenty-two seats, one shared roast, and a quiet bookshop next door we'll wander to between courses, when the rain agrees.

data.title:
An evening
for the rain.
data.body: A long winter dinner in a converted printing room above a bookshop. One shared roast, an unhurried wine list, and a single intermission that may, if the weather agrees, become a walk to the harbour and back.
details: A printing room, Bairro Alto · Lisbon
From eight, well into the evening

data.title:
See you
at the table.
data.body: Every Long Table evening is by application. We read each one, and we usually answer within a week. The next room opens for Brooklyn on the seventeenth of January.
footer: By Iris & Theo, 2022, in a borrowed kitchen in Lisbon.
In Bricolage Grotesque & Fraunces, with one rust-red ink.
Dress for the rain. Bring a hand-written question.
